I pulled the policy snapshot and the runtime logs. Quick summary (high level):

- Root cause hypothesis: the "burst safety_valve" we introduced as a hard-fail protection is being triggered incorrectly for NimblePay due to a percentile calculation edge-case in the burst window code path. When the per-minute token estimate crosses the configured burst_capacity threshold, the valve flips and routes requests into a throttled path that returns 429s while it rebuilds the token bucket.
- Evidence: logs show safety_valve toggles at 2028-09-27T09:04:58Z correlated with a sharp but short-lived increase in concurrent token requests. We also see a policy file change around 2028-09-20 that reduced the customer-specific burst window from 120s -> 60s (rate_policy_snapshot.json attached).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (safe order):
1) Apply a targeted override for NimblePay to temporarily increase burst window to 180s and bump burst_capacity by 30% (policy RP-9082-override). (est. 10 min to push)
2) Disable the hard-fail safety_valve on the customer policy and switch to soft-backpressure for 24h while we validate. (requires config rollback — est. 20 min)
3) Post-mortem: revert the percentile calc bug and add an integration test that simulates large short bursts. (next-day work)

I can push 1) + 2) with Ops approval now. We should also confirm with NimblePay whether they can tolerate the temporary increased burst caps during their 02:00 UTC batch.

Attachments: rate_policy_snapshot.json

Team / Sam / Priya — finalizing the short remediation plan and owners. Looping Marissa for executive visibility given potential SLA/credit asks.

What happened (tl;dr):
- A customer-specific change to the burst window reduced the smoothing period (120s -> 60s) and exposed a percentile-calculation edge-case in the burst safety_valve. Short intense bursts temporarily flipped the safety valve, putting requests on an aggressive throttled path and causing 429s and elevated p95.

Immediate actions taken (completed):
- 09/27 17:20 PDT — Marcus pushed RP-9082-override to increase the burst window to 180s and raise burst_capacity by 30%. (rolled to NimblePay only)
- 09/27 17:35 PDT — Disabled hard-fail safety_valve for NimblePay and enabled soft backpressure mode.
- We monitored until 02:30 UTC during their batch window and observed p95 return to 220–380ms with 0.2% 429s in the test cohort (sampled).

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Marcus: produce a code fix for percentile calc bug + integration test (ETA: 2028-09-30 COB).
- Dylan: prepare a short customer-facing incident note and compliance summary; include the temporary policy delta and monitoring evidence (ETA: 2028-09-29 EOD).
- Irene: coordinate any commercial remediation (credits/waiver) after we validate full regression testing (ETA: 2028-10-02).
